top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B001) rewards one identifiable discovery: firms differ in productivity and select into exporting and foreign investment, which makes reallocation across firms a channel for the gains from trade. The mechanism and its exports-versus-FDI sorting implication have been tested against firm-level data in many countries for over twenty years, and where the baseline failed in detail the literature extended it. The attribution to the two named laureates is defensible, since Melitz supplied the canonical selection model and Helpman the sorting result and the monopolistic-competition foundations. The main risk is that Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum and Redding are not credited on this entry. I judge that manageable with a narrow citation that names selection and reallocation, claims no settled welfare magnitudes and does not claim the whole firm-level trade literature, with the empirical precursors acknowledged in the scientific background. The slate offers only P001 or no award. I rank P001 above P000 because the achievement is mature and substantial and the attribution gap does not justify withholding the prize. I do not treat the unanimity of the supporters as evidence of merit.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile: no tie to Helpman or Melitz, and my frequent co-authors (Bayer, Anwar, Lindquist, Holmlund, Lochner, Bindler) are not credited on the proposal. I note a field-adjacent interest in labour economics, but the labour entry (B030) is not on the slate. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
